newsitem.title: IRAQ: Anti-aicraft fire said launched from Baghdad.
newsitem.headline: Anti-aicraft fire said launched from Baghdad.

text.p: Anti-aircraft fire was launched from positions in Baghdad on Tuesday, eywitnesses said.
It was not immediately clear what the fire was aimed at, but earlier the United States said it had launched a cruise missile strike on Iraq in retaliation for Iraqi attacks in its Kurdish north.
Iraqi state-run radio and television interrupted programmes on Tuesday and broadcast national songs, an indication that something unusual had occurred.
But there remained no official confirmation of the attacks and life in Baghdad remained normal.

Earlier in Washington, U.S. defence officials, who asked not to be identified, said the unmanned and highly accurate missiles were fired from B-52 bombers and American warships in the Gulf at military targets in and around Baghdad.

The United States last sent cruise missiles against Iraq in June 1993 to avenge an alleged plot to kill former U.S. president George Bush during a visit to Kuwait. The attacks then killed six civilians.
